transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-03
Start time: 18:30 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Mike Chen (Aurora CTO), Sara Lopez (ML Eng), Tom Rivera (Head of DevOps)

Summary: quick discovery on PLG/self-serve API, quickstart free credits, comparing hosted vs dedicated vs private for a mid-stage analytics startup.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, i'm Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account, with priya our SE, how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Mike: good, thanks, yeah excited to learn more, we got your email about the quickstart credits, so wanted to understand time to first token and what a typical eval looks like.
[00:14] Jordan: totally, that's what we'll cover — quickstart, the free credits, and then a bit on deployment options once you decide whether hosted is enough or you want dedicated or private.
[00:22] Priya: hi team, quick note from my side, i'm going to ask a few infra questions so we can scope any benchmarks and POC, and i'll share a proposed runbook afterwards.
[00:33] Sara: great, we mostly care about latency for live features and cost per token for batch embedding jobs.
[00:40] Tom: and for us ops-wise, VPC peering and KMS integration are must-haves if we go non-hosted.
[00:48] Jordan: understood. quick q: you're currently prototyping with openai or self-hosted?
[00:52] Mike: currently prototyping with OpenAI for generative and Replicate for some model hosting, but cost is creeping up so wanted to see alternatives.
[01:02] Priya: cool — typical pattern we see: teams start with Hosted (Redwood API) via self-serve, use free credits to validate, then if they need isolation or predictable throughput they move to Dedicated, and for strict compliance or on-prem they look at Private (VPC/on-prem).
[01:15] Jordan: for PLG quickstarts we try to make time-to-first-token under 10 minutes if they follow the quickstart, the SDK and sample repo get you going fast.
[01:23] Sara: nice, is that including model download or just the hosted endpoint?
[01:27] Priya: for hosted it's endpoint — you don't need to manage models. time to first token really just depends on API key and SDK setup. for dedicated/private there is more setup time — hours to days depending on networking.
[01:40] Mike: and what about the free credits — how much, and any guardrails?
[01:44] Jordan: we give a starter credit bundle for PLG signups — the exact amount can vary, i'll include the redemption link in the follow-up, there's also quotas and rate limits applied by default.
[01:53] Sara: can you outline what we'd need to do to measure latency for our user flows?
[01:58] Priya: yep, we'll share a benchmark plan: sample prompts, sequence lengths, embedding sizes, and recommended models/quantization profiles. for quick tests use the hosted api and our streaming responses to measure p99 latency.
[02:10] Tom: for our e2e tests we need KV cache behavior — some transcripts mentioned KV cash in earlier notes, is that the same as KV cache?
[02:18] Priya: yes, it's KV cache — apologies if the automated notes spell it odd sometimes. that matters for long-context usage and to keep latency low.
[02:26] Jordan: do you have SLOs in mind for latency and cost targets?
[02:30] Mike: for interactive features we want p99 < 300ms for short prompts, for embeddings batch jobs cost < $0.02 per 1k vectors (rough target).
[02:40] Priya: got it. on hosted you can often hit those latency numbers with optimized models and streaming; for consistent p99 you'd look at Dedicated with reserved pools.
[02:51] Mike: what's involved to try Dedicated? do we need to sign a contract?
[02:55] Jordan: Dedicated is generally reserved capacity and typically involves a monthly commitment; we can do a short-term eval but for full reserved pricing it's contract-based. you can still prototype on hosted and then move to Dedicated when ready.
[03:06] Sara: what about data residency and audit logs? we have european customers and need logs and retention controls.
[03:13] Priya: Redwood supports region pinning for hosted and Dedicated in many cases; Private gives you full control. audit logs, token-level traces and exportable logs are available — we'll include the specifics in the security pack.
[03:26] Tom: KMS integration — we want to bring our own keys, HSM preferred.
[03:30] Priya: BYOK with KMS/HSM is supported in Private deployments and in some Dedicated setups. hosted can integrate with customer KMS in select enterprise agreements. we'll detail options in the doc.
[03:42] Mike: okay, curious about the dev experience — SDKs, quickstart repo, notebooks?
[03:46] Jordan: we have language SDKs (python/node), example notebooks, and a quickstart repo. the typical flow: sign up, redeem credits, generate API key, run one-of-the-sample notebooks — we also provide a Postman collection.
[03:59] Sara: any friction we've seen with time-to-first-token? like SSO, SAML, or provisioning delays?
[04:04] Priya: for self-serve it's minimal — SSO only comes into play for org-managed accounts; if you register with email you can get keys immediately. for org-level onboarding we do SAML/SCIM and that adds setup time.
[04:16] Mike: we'd likely start with quickstart under a single account then graduate to org-managed with SSO.
[04:21] Priya: that's common. also note rate limits on free trials can affect large batch jobs — we'll recommend small-scale tests first.
[04:31] Jordan: demo question — are you interested in a live demo of quickstart or would you rather try self-serve first?
[04:36] Mike: i'd like to try self-serve first, but schedule a deep-dive if we run into infra questions.
[04:42] Jordan: perfect. i'll also include a short video walk-through link.
[04:46] Sara: about benchmarking — we need to run both latency and throughput tests; can priya help define scripts?
[04:51] Priya: yes i'll share a benchmark script — we'll include curl/python examples and a busy-worker script for throughput. recommend using hosted for initial runs, then run same tests on Dedicated to compare.
[05:03] Tom: regarding costs — is there tooling to estimate per-token cost with batching and quantization?
[05:08] Priya: Redwood Optimize gives recommendations for batching and quantization, and the Console shows token-level cost breakdowns per route/model. we'll include screenshots.
[05:18] Mike: security question again — SOC2 and penetration test results?
[05:22] Jordan: yes we are SOC 2 Type II, and we can provide a redacted report and our pen test summary in the security pack.
[05:30] Sara: great. also need to confirm data retention policies for trial data.
[05:34] Priya: retention defaults to 30 days for trial accounts, enterprise can request retention changes and archival policies — details in the pack.
[05:42] Jordan: ok let's run through a suggested plan: 1) Jordan sends credits + quickstart links; 2) Customer tries quickstart and reports time-to-first-token; 3) Priya provides benchmark plan and security docs; 4) schedule SE deep-dive for network setup and Dedicated/Private scoping. sound right?
[05:58] Mike: yep, sounds good. do you have an example of POC timeline?
[06:02] Priya: typical POC 2-4 weeks: week 1 quickstart and baseline latencies, week 2 run batch embedding cost tests, week 3 iterate and tune quantization/batching, week 4 decision and if needed Dedicated onboarding.
[06:16] Sara: what about model choices — are we locked to particular open models?
[06:20] Priya: we provide a curated catalog of open models and Redwood-verified performance profiles; we also support model variants and quantization-friendly builds. if you need a custom model we can help onboard it.
[06:31] Mike: any gotchas with long-context use cases?
[06:34] Priya: long context needs KV cache management and sometimes different kernels; those are supported, but latency tradeoffs exist. we'll point to best practices.
[06:44] Jordan: can you commit to trying the quickstart before next thursday?
[06:47] Mike: yes i'll aim for that, sara and tom will try the SDK snippets.
[06:51] Priya: i'll block time for a deep-dive next week, what days work?
[06:56] Tom: tuesday or wednesday afternoon pacific works.
[07:00] Jordan: great — i'll propose tuesday 3pm PT in the follow-up.
[07:04] Mike: any concerns about migration from hosted to dedicated later? is it disruptive?
[07:09] Priya: migration is planned — you can pin model versions and rollouts, and we have automatic fallback policies. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and isolation; we help with the cutover.
[07:20] Sara: notes on monitoring — do you have tracing hooks and per-route dashboards?
[07:24] Priya: yes Redwood Console has per-route/model dashboards, traces, and error analysis; you can export metrics to your monitoring stack.
[07:33] Jordan: ok last quick Q: who else needs to be looped in from your side for procurement or security?
[07:37] Mike: our security lead will eventually be involved, currently it's me, sara and tom. procurement may join once we commit.
[07:43] Jordan: copy that. we'll send the security pack and pricing and circle back after you try quickstart.
[07:48] Mike: sounds good, thanks.
[07:50] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and action items.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcription has occasional mis-hearings (KV cash) and speaker overlaps, representative of automated Fireflies export. Link references included in follow-up rather than typed in transcript: quickstart repo, pricing sheet, security pack (SOC2, pen test summary), benchmark plan.
